name: Beyond Parallel 436 Sanctioned Markets Database
publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
description: Exhaustive geolocated survey of 436 officially sanctioned North Korean markets (jangmadang) with physical footprints, estimated vendor stall counts, and calculated state rent revenues.
coverage: 2018; nationwide North Korea across all 9 provinces and special cities
last_updated_evidence: Report publication date and Carto table creation timestamp in metadata
presentation: Shown on a legacy Leaflet/Carto embed with basic revenue range slider; slow to render, lacks modern vector styling, satellite overlay alignment, and linkage to current prices.
build_idea: Directly ingest the 421 geocoded points into our MapLibre Atlas layer, letting users hover any market to see satellite footprint, stall capacity, and municipal revenue.
notes: 421 points have exact coordinates; remaining 15 have Daily NK stall estimates. Secondary table 'dprkadminall' in same Carto account provides matching county/provincial population polygons.

name: North Korea Uncovered (Google Earth KML/KMZ)
publisher: Curtis Melvin / North Korean Economy Watch
description: Seminal crowdsourced geographic database of North Korea containing thousands of annotated placemarks for markets, industrial complexes, mines, railways, and commercial nodes.
last_updated_evidence: Final version release date published on NKEconWatch before merging into 38 North Digital Atlas
presentation: Only viewable by opening monolithic KMZ files in desktop Google Earth; crashes modern web viewers and has no tabular search or API.
build_idea: Extract commercial, mining, and light industrial folders from the KMZ to backfill historical market and factory names for our interactive atlas.
notes: Forms the historical bedrock of North Korean commercial and logistical mapping, widely cited by academia and UN panels.

name: #AccessDPRK Geospatial Mapping Project
description: Massive continuation and expansion of North Korea open-source GIS mapping, cataloging over 70,500 sites including markets, factories, state stores, mines, rail facilities, and security outposts.
last_updated_evidence: 2023 Edition release notes on project page, supplemented by regular 2024-2026 Patreon map updates
update_cadence: annual major release with quarterly updates
license: Proprietary research (free basic tier, paid Pro tier via Patreon)
presentation: Distributed as heavy Google Earth KMZ bundles that require desktop Google Earth Pro to navigate and lack programmatic web search.
build_idea: Convert commercial, economic, and industrial sub-layers into GeoJSON layers for our MapLibre viewer, enabling pinpoint identification of factories and distribution centres.
notes: The largest publicly known single point-of-interest collection for North Korean civil, industrial, and economic infrastructure.

name: Daily NK Bi-Weekly Market Price & Currency Indicators
description: Bi-weekly field survey of consumer market prices and exchange rates collected by secret reporting partners across three major commercial hubs: Pyongyang, Sinuiju, and Hyesan.
last_updated_evidence: Post ID 325948 published 2026-10-01 detailing September 27 price survey
license: Copyright Daily NK (open REST API access)
presentation: Published as narrative news articles with inline prose prices and occasional static chart images; no interactive time-series explorer or CSV export.
build_idea: Build an automated scraper over the WP-JSON API to parse grain (rice, corn), currency (USD/KPW, RMB/KPW), and fuel (gasoline, diesel) prices into continuous interactive charts linked to city map markers.
notes: Gold standard ground-truth dataset for domestic food security, hyperinflation, and marketization in North Korea.

name: Daily NK Korean Market Price Database (데일리NK 시장물가)
description: Original Korean-language source for Daily NK regular market surveys, including detailed commodity breakdowns for cooking oil, sugar, pork, and diesel alongside staple grains.
last_updated_evidence: Latest Korean market report verified via WP-JSON API tag 797 (쌀/rice) and 234 (장마당/market)
presentation: Narrative blog posts with tables embedded as static HTML; requires regex scraping to isolate numerical price figures.
build_idea: Feed Korean-language price tags to capture supplementary commodity series (pork, flour, cooking oil, coal) omitted from English digests.
notes: Tag 234 (장마당) contains 321 posts, tag 797 (쌀) has 187 posts, tag 984 (옥수수) has 165 posts.

name: Asia Press / Rimjin-gang Undercover Market Price Survey
publisher: Asia Press International (アジアプレス / リムジンガン)
description: In-depth investigative field reporting and undercover price surveys conducted in northern border cities (Hyesan, Musan, Hoeryong) focusing on state enterprise wages, inflation, and black market currency rates.
coverage: 2008-2026; Ryanggang Province (Hyesan) and North Hamgyong Province (Musan, Hoeryong)
last_updated_evidence: Part 8 of Large-Scale Price Investigation published September 11, 2026
presentation: Longform investigative articles with high-resolution border photography and interview excerpts; lacks downloadable time series.
build_idea: Overlay Asia Press wage and hyperinflation field surveys alongside Daily NK market prices to visualize real purchasing power collapse.
notes: Japanese edition at asiapress.org/ap2/ features identical data with occasional additional interviews from reporting partners inside North Korea.

name: NK Pro DPRK Economic Database & Market Price Index
description: Proprietary analytical index tracking market commodity prices, domestic currency devaluation, state distribution rationing, and macroeconomic trends.
last_updated_evidence: Recent editorial briefs on NK Pro tracking autumn harvest price indices
presentation: Gated web dashboard with interactive charts; high analytical quality but inaccessible to open-source users without subscription.
build_idea: Use NK Pro methodology as a benchmark to validate our open scrapers built on Daily NK and UN Comtrade.
notes: High barrier to entry due to expensive professional paywall, but valuable as an analytical reference.

name: UN Comtrade China-DPRK Bilateral Trade API
description: Official bilateral customs merchandise trade data reported by China (Reporter 156) for North Korea (Partner 408) broken down by HS code, trade flow (export/import), net weight, and FOB value.
last_updated_evidence: Verified 2023-2024 annual and monthly records returned via public preview API
license: UN Data License / Public Access (fair use preview)
presentation: API requires understanding reporter/partner country codes; web portal is bulky and does not show dedicated DPRK smuggling or sanctions overlays.
build_idea: Create an interactive trade flow chart on the site showing top Chinese exports (grain, vegetable oil, machinery) and illicit sanctioned imports (coal, textiles, minerals).
notes: Free public preview endpoint returns up to 500 rows per call without authentication; monthly data queryable using freqCode=M.

name: China Customs (GACC) Monthly Trade Statistics Platform
publisher: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (海关总署)
description: Primary authoritative origin of all China-DPRK trade data, publishing monthly bilateral export and import totals in RMB and USD by partner country and HS 8-digit commodity code.
endpoint: http://43.248.49.97/ (Online Query Platform / 进出口商品国别总值表)
last_updated_evidence: August 2026 monthly customs bulletin release date
presentation: Bare IP query platform with strict session timeouts and CAPTCHAs, making automated scraping brittle.
build_idea: Scrape monthly top-line numbers as an early-warning signal for trade border re-openings before UN Comtrade consolidates.
notes: Chinese language only ('朝鲜' partner code 110). Mirror statistics from GACC account for >90% of North Korea's total legal trade.

name: KOTRA Annual North Korea External Trade Trends Report (북한 대외무역동향)
description: Annual flagship South Korean government intelligence report evaluating North Korea's total foreign trade, trade balance, major trading partners, and top export/import items.
last_updated_evidence: 2025 report published late July 2026 showing $3.13 billion total trade
license: Korea Open Government License (KOGL Type 1: Open Access)
presentation: Packaged as a 100+ page static PDF publication with embedded data tables; impossible to query interactively online.
build_idea: Digitize KOTRA's annual partner country trade matrix into an interactive world map showing North Korea's shifting trade reliance from Europe/Asia to China and Russia.
notes: Excludes inter-Korean trade. The 2025 trade volume reached $3.128B (+16.0% YoY), with China accounting for >98% of total recorded trade.

name: KOSIS North Korea External Trade Time Series (KOSIS 북한통계포털)
description: Official statistical database providing digitized time-series tables of North Korea's total external trade, export/import balances, and country breakdowns based on KOTRA and UN data.
endpoint: https://kosis.kr/openapi/ (KOSIS OpenAPI North Korea Trade Tables)
last_updated_evidence: Statistical update reflecting 2025 KOTRA trade survey in KOSIS portal
presentation: Standard government statistical table interface; customizable and exportable to CSV/XLSX, but isolated from geographic map context.
build_idea: Pull verified multi-decade trade statistics via KOSIS Open API to display long-term historical trade collapses (1991 Soviet collapse, 2017 sanctions, 2020 COVID).
notes: KOSIS Open API allows programmatic JSON queries with public API key.

name: Bank of Korea North Korea GDP Growth & Sectoral Estimates (북한 경제성장률 추정 결과)
description: Authoritative annual macroeconomic calculation estimating North Korea's real GDP growth rate, nominal Gross National Income (GNI), per capita income, and sector-by-sector output.
coverage: 1990-2025; annual sectoral breakdown (agriculture, mining, manufacturing, services)
last_updated_evidence: Official press release published July 31, 2026 estimating 2025 real GDP growth at +3.5%
presentation: Published as PDF press releases with comprehensive statistical tables; highly cited worldwide but lacks an interactive digital database.
build_idea: Construct an interactive macroeconomic overview panel showing industrial output swings (heavy vs light industry, mining, agriculture) over Kim Jong Un's rule.
notes: Uses UN System of National Accounts (SNA) with South Korean price weights; 2024 growth was +3.7% and 2025 was +3.5%.

name: ITC Trade Map North Korea Mirror Trade Portal
description: Global mirror trade statistics platform detailing imports and exports for Democratic People's Republic of Korea reported by partner countries across 5,300 HS 6-digit product groups.
coverage: 2001-2025; North Korea and all UN member partner countries
last_updated_evidence: ITC quarterly database refresh timestamp
license: ITC Terms of Use (free registration required for bulk download)
presentation: Traditional ASP.NET web tables with complex session cookies; data is rich but difficult to automate without headless browsers.
build_idea: Use to detect secondary trading partners beyond China (e.g. Russia, African states, Southeast Asia).
notes: Crucial for identifying non-Chinese trade partners who report bilateral commerce to international bodies.

name: UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List (1718 Committee)
description: Official machine-readable XML feed of all individuals and corporate entities designated by the UN Security Council 1718 Sanctions Committee on North Korea for asset freezes and travel bans.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live XML file (2.18 MB) containing 80 DPRK individuals and 75 DPRK entities
update_cadence: frozen since Russian veto in April 2024 (no new designations added)
presentation: Monolithic raw XML file; clean and structured, but contains no graphical search, relationship links, or vessel IMO indexing.
build_idea: Ingest directly into our sanctions explorer to show UN-designated entities, their aliases, and their historical connection to illicit procurement networks.
notes: Features 80 individuals and 75 entities. XML schema includes nationality, passport numbers, aliases, and exact Security Council committee justification.

name: US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) DPRK Entries
description: United States unilateral sanctions database containing hundreds of North Korean regime officials, military front companies, banks, cyber threat actors (Lazarus), and designated vessels.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live XML file (29.18 MB) containing 544 DPRK entries and 105 named merchant vessels
update_cadence: real-time as designations are declared (multiple times monthly)
presentation: Available as a 29MB XML, CSV, or web search tool; lacks network visualization and interactive geographic mapping of ship ports.
build_idea: Extract all 105 named vessels (with IMO/MMSI numbers) and digital currency wallet addresses to drive our vessel tracking and cyber theft explorer.
notes: Includes famous interdicted vessels: Chong Chon Gang, Am Nok Gang, Baek Ma Kang, Dai Hong Dan, Hwang Gum San 2.

name: UK Sanctions List (FCDO DPRK Regime)
description: Official UK consolidated sanctions list covering individuals, entities, and ships designated under The Democratic People's Republic of Korea (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.
last_updated_evidence: Verified CSV header 'Report Date: 01-Oct-2026' with 50 MB total dataset
presentation: Clean downloadable CSV and XML updated every single business day; well maintained since OFSI consolidated list was retired in January 2026.
build_idea: Cross-reference UK designations against UN and OFAC lists to highlight unilateral sanctions divergences and British enforcement targets.
notes: Supersedes the legacy OFSI list (which permanently closed January 28, 2026). Published in CSV, XML, HTML, ODS, and TXT.

name: EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (DPRK Regime)
publisher: European External Action Service (EEAS) / DG FISMA
description: European Union sanctions database listing all individuals, military entities, and trade enterprises subject to asset freezes and autonomous EU restrictive measures against North Korea.
last_updated_evidence: Artifact timestamp 20261001145703-cgg on OpenSanctions daily sync
license: EU Legal Notice / Open Data (CC BY 4.0)
presentation: Official European Commission server frequently drops connections (HTTP 503); OpenSanctions mirror provides reliable daily JSON-LD stream.
build_idea: Harmonize EU autonomous designations with US OFAC and UN lists into our consolidated search engine.
notes: Includes autonomous EU listings not present on UN consolidated list, particularly European front companies and logistics intermediaries.

name: Japan MOF & METI Sanctions Lists (北朝鮮に対する制裁措置)
publisher: Japan Ministry of Finance & Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
description: Japan's autonomous economic sanctions list and METI End-User List designating North Korean financial entities, weapons procurement fronts, and Chongryon-affiliated entities.
coverage: 2006-2026; Japan unilateral measures and UN implementation
last_updated_evidence: OpenSanctions daily scrape verified updated 2026-10-01T10:36:56 with 2,788 targets
presentation: Official MOFA/METI pages publish PDFs and Kanpo (official gazette) notices; OpenSanctions harmonizes them into structured JSON.
build_idea: Highlight Japan-specific designations involving maritime shipping bans and illicit financial remittance channels linked to Chongryon.
notes: METI End User List (jp_meti_eul) targets 825 global entities suspected of WMD proliferation, including dozens in Pyongyang.

name: South Korea KOSTI Unilateral Sanctions & Watchlist (무역안보관리원 대북제재)
description: South Korean government comprehensive repository of unilateral sanctions targets (독자제재 명단) and high-risk trading entities under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act.
last_updated_evidence: Recent unilateral designations of Russian vessels and DPRK logistics coordinators
update_cadence: sporadic (updated upon each government designation announcement)
presentation: Available as textual news summaries and PDF appendices; lacks open JSON API.
build_idea: Track South Korea's autonomous sanctions expanding to Russia-DPRK arms shipping vessels and front companies.
notes: KOSTI (formerly Strategic Trade Institute / 전략물자관리원) maintains compliance guides for South Korean financial and shipping firms.

name: OpenSanctions Unified DPRK Sanctions & Maritime Dataset
description: Open-source intelligence engine consolidating and deduplicating North Korean entities across UN, US OFAC, EU, UK, Japan, Swiss SECO, Canadian, and Australian sanctions registries into FollowTheMoney format.
coverage: 1995-2026; global sanctions against North Korea and affiliates
last_updated_evidence: Daily automated pipeline updated multiple times daily across all official feeds
presentation: Outstanding graph schema with entity cross-referencing, IMO numbers, and known aliases; downloadable as streaming JSON lines.
build_idea: Use as our primary backend sanctions ingest pipeline to instantly keep all international designations synchronized with zero manual scraping.
notes: FollowTheMoney (FtM) standard allows painless querying of vessels, corporate beneficial owners, and aliases.

name: RUSI / Korea Risk Group DPRK Reports Sanctions-Evasion Database
publisher: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) & Korea Risk Group
description: Exhaustive structured database compiling over a decade of UN Panel of Experts reports into 26,187 entities, 753 vessels with IMO numbers, 2,306 companies, and 58,267 investigated relationships.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live OpenAPI 3.1 specification at https://dprk-reports.org/.well-known/openapi.json
update_cadence: frozen at final UN Panel mandate expiry (2024)
presentation: World-class REST API and web graph explorer; provides direct proof citations to exact paragraphs and annexes in UN Panel reports.
build_idea: Integrate directly into our Atlas to let users query any North Korean ship, front company, or coal smuggling network and see its entire illicit ownership graph.
notes: Includes 753 vessels, 2,090 persons, 1,023 interdiction events, and full pathfinding between entities via /api/paths.

name: UN Security Council 1718 Panel of Experts Reports Archive
description: Complete collection of biannual final and midterm investigation reports (2010–2024) documenting ship-to-ship petroleum transfers, coal smuggling, overseas workers, and cyber heists.
last_updated_evidence: Final Panel of Experts report S/2024/171 before Russian veto ended panel mandate on April 30, 2024
presentation: Scattered across heavy 300-page UN PDF documents with low-resolution satellite screenshots and unindexed tables.
build_idea: Extract coordinates of documented ship-to-ship (STS) transfer locations in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea into an interactive smuggling hotspot heat map.
notes: Mandate vetoed by Russia in March 2024. Succeeded by the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT).

name: Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) Reports & API
publisher: Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (11 Member States)
description: Official independent monitoring body established in October 2024 by US, South Korea, Japan, UK, France, Germany, and partners to succeed the vetoed UN Panel of Experts.
coverage: 2024-2026; North Korea sanctions violations, arms transfers, cyber theft, overseas labor
last_updated_evidence: Report MSMT/2026/1 on DPRK overseas labor published September 16, 2026
presentation: Modern Vite SPA with dedicated backend REST API at /api/post/list and /api/post/detail providing direct PDF attachment downloads.
build_idea: Scrape MSMT reports via its JSON API to track contemporary post-2024 sanctions evasions, Russian ammunition transfers, and overseas worker operations across 17 host nations.
notes: First report (May 2025) covered Russia-DPRK military cooperation; second (Oct 2025) covered cyber/crypto; third (Sept 2026) covered overseas labor generating $450M-$800M/year.

name: Global Fishing Watch North Korea Dark Fishing Fleet Dataset
description: Landmark scientific dataset combining satellite radar (SAR), optical imagery, and night lights (VIIRS) to identify ~900 Chinese dark fishing vessels operating illegally in North Korean waters.
coverage: 2017-2019; North Korean Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Sea of Japan
last_updated_evidence: Published in Science Advances July 2020 with open GitHub replication code and figures
presentation: Provided as raw Python scripts and supplementary data in GitHub repo; requires processing to reproject onto interactive maps.
build_idea: Render the illegal fishing tracks as an interactive maritime layer showing the massive depletion of squid stocks in North Korean waters.
notes: Revealed illegal catch estimated at over 160,000 metric tons worth hundreds of millions of dollars, violating UN sanctions prohibiting fish trade.

name: NK Pro Maritime Vessel Tracker
description: Specialized maritime tracking system integrating AIS telemetry, satellite radar, Port State Control inspections, and Equasis ownership data for North Korean and sanctioned merchant ships.
coverage: 2016-2026; East Asia maritime routes, Nampo, Chongjin, Vostochny (Russia), Zhoushan (China)
last_updated_evidence: Live real-time AIS pings and ongoing vessel profile updates
presentation: Interactive Leaflet web map tracking live ship movements, flag history, and ownership changes behind enterprise paywall.
build_idea: Use verified IMO numbers from NK Pro investigations to query free OpenSanctions maritime profiles and public AIS endpoints.
notes: Identified the primary cargo vessels ferrying North Korean artillery munitions to Russian Far East ports (e.g. Angara, Maria).

name: Tayvano / Lazarus & BlueNoroff Cyber Theft Research Repository
description: Comprehensive open-source repository chronicling 301 distinct cyber heists, cryptocurrency drainings, social engineering campaigns, and wallet addresses attributed to DPRK state hackers.
coverage: 2017-2026; global crypto exchanges, DeFi protocols, and developer victims
last_updated_evidence: Incident file trtr-2026-unknown.md documented August 28, 2026 ($18,000,000 theft)
presentation: Structured markdown files organized chronologically with dates, stolen amounts, C2 domains, transaction hashes, and victim wallet addresses.
build_idea: Build a live 'Lazarus Cyber Revenue Timeline' quantifying cumulative crypto theft (over $3.5B) directly funding North Korea's ballistic missile programs.
notes: 13 separate heist incidents documented in 2026 alone. Includes BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, and FakeRecruiter campaign IOCs.

name: FBI Lazarus Cyber Crime & Cryptocurrency Public Advisories
description: Official US law enforcement advisories and press releases detailing major state-sponsored crypto heists (Harmony Horizon, Stake.com, Ronin) with clusters of attributed blockchain addresses.
last_updated_evidence: Formal FBI alert on DPRK social engineering attacks targeting crypto developers
update_cadence: sporadic (published following major indictments or seizure actions)
presentation: Plaintext press statements with wallet lists embedded in article body; high legal certainty but not offered as machine-readable JSON feeds.
build_idea: Parse official FBI wallet clusters into an interactive address watchlist showing fund consolidation and mixing patterns.
notes: August 2023 alert identified 6 Bitcoin wallets holding 1,580 BTC (~$40M at the time) from Alphapo, CoinsPaid, and Atomic Wallet.

name: ZachXBT Lazarus On-Chain Forensic Investigations
description: Independent blockchain forensic investigations tracing Lazarus Group laundering networks, peel chains, cross-chain bridge hops, and mixer deposits (Tornado Cash, Sinbad, Blender).
coverage: 2021-2026; on-chain laundering trails across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and TRON
last_updated_evidence: Attribution of 2025-2026 centralized exchange exploits and laundering networks
presentation: Distributed across X threads, Telegram channels, and Dune Analytics dashboards; highly detailed on-chain graphs but fragmented.
build_idea: Aggregate ZachXBT's verified Lazarus addresses into an address intelligence tool with links to block explorers.
notes: Instrumental in attributing the $1.5B Bybit hack in early 2025 and tracking laundering across OTC desks in East Asia.

name: Geofabrik Daily North Korea OpenStreetMap Extracts
description: Daily updated vector spatial database of North Korea containing all mapped infrastructure: complete railway lines, railway stations, power plants, substations, ports, mines, and roads.
last_updated_evidence: File north-korea-260929.osm.pbf verified at 92.4 MB with Last-Modified header 2026-09-29
license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)
presentation: Pre-packaged PBF (88.1 MB) and Shapefile ZIP (234.4 MB) archives; clean, topologically consistent, and ready for GIS pipelines.
build_idea: Extract infrastructure layers (railways, power grid, mines, ports) directly into vector tiles for our MapLibre base map.
notes: Historical daily archive goes back to 2015, enabling spatial diffing of new railway branches and industrial construction over the Kim Jong Un era.

name: I-RENK North Korean Mines & Mineral Deposits Database (북한지하자원넷)
publisher: South-North Korea Exchanges & Cooperation Support Association (SONOSA) & KOMIR
description: Specialized South Korean government portal providing a structured database of 112 major North Korean mines with Korean names, aliases, administrative county locations, and primary/secondary mineral deposits.
last_updated_evidence: Verified live query returning 112 mines (78 metallic, 14 non-metallic, 20 coal) and 2026 newsletter archives
license: Copyright SONOSA (South-North Korea Exchanges and Cooperation Support Association)
presentation: Tabular HTML database with filterable drop-downs by mineral and province, accompanied by a downloadable nationwide mineral belt map graphic.
build_idea: Geocode the 112 mines using their administrative county and satellite imagery to create an interactive natural resources map (Musan iron ore, Komdok zinc, Dancheon magnesite).
notes: Includes detailed coverage of rare earth, tungsten, molybdenum, magnesite, and anthracite coal mines.

name: USGS Minerals Yearbook: North Korea
description: Authoritative annual US geological survey detailing North Korea's mineral production volumes, mineral trade to China, and Table 2 listing major mines, processing facilities, capacities, and locations.
last_updated_evidence: 2022 Minerals Yearbook tables-only advance release XLSX
presentation: Clean XLSX spreadsheets and PDF reports; very clear production estimates but released with typical 2-year government publication delay.
build_idea: Combine USGS production capacity figures with I-RENK mine locations to show annual tonnage potential for major mining complexes.
notes: Covers coal, iron ore, lead, zinc, magnesite, tungsten, cement, and refined copper.

name: Kim Jong Un 'Regional Development 20×10' Factory Construction Tracker (지방발전 20×10)
publisher: 38 North (Stimson Center) & Daily NK / Rodong Sinmun
description: Tracking dataset of North Korea's 10-year policy (2024–2033) building modernized light industry, food, and clothing factories across 20 selected counties per year, combining satellite imagery and state media announcements.
endpoint: https://www.38north.org/ (Satellite monitoring series by Peter Makowsky and Martyn Williams)
coverage: 2024-2026; 20 designated counties in 2024 and 20 counties in 2025 across all provinces
last_updated_evidence: Satellite tracking of 2024 site completions and 2025 hospital/service complex groundbreakings
presentation: Individual satellite imagery articles analyzing construction speed, land use (farmland conversion), and material shortages.
build_idea: Plot all 20 counties from the 2024 batch (Sukchon, Songchon, Kusong, Unsan, Kujang, etc.) and 2025 batch with before/after satellite imagery pins showing state-directed industrial investment.
notes: First year focused on light industrial three-factory formula; expanded in 2025 to include regional hospitals, grain depots, and sci-tech hubs.

name: MOU North Korea Special Economic Zones & Development Zones Database (경제특구·경제개발구)
description: Comprehensive South Korean Ministry of Unification registry cataloging all 29 designated special economic zones (10 central-level SEZs including Rason, Kaesong, Sinuiju, Wonsan-Kalma, and 19 provincial-level development zones).
coverage: 1991-2026; 29 designated economic zones across all provinces
last_updated_evidence: Ministry of Unification theme update on 29 economic development zones under the Economic Development Zone Law
presentation: Well structured informational portal with legal summaries, tax concession rules, target industrial sectors, and geographic boundaries.
build_idea: Map all 29 SEZ/EDZ boundary polygons on our Atlas, color-coded by development status (operational like Rason vs paper zones like Kangnyong Green Model Zone).
notes: Covers high-profile zones (Rason, Kaesong, Sinuiju, Hwanggumpyong) and obscure provincial zones (Unjong High-Tech, Hyondong Industrial, Onsong Island Tourism).
